headline: Leo Carlsson, offered by Flyers, burns Philly in Ducks' win
take:
ESPN reports that Leo Carlsson scored and assisted on the game-winner in the Ducks' 5-4 win over the Flyers, the team that offered him a contract last summer. As The Athletic's Kevin Kurz posted a day earlier, Carlsson reflected on the Flyers' offer sheet, saying "I'm grateful that they thought of me as that player."

The revenge storyline is fun, but our numbers say the bigger point is how Carlsson is producing. He has 3 goals and 10 assists in 11 games so far this season, yet the Ducks have controlled only 47 percent of the chances with him on the ice at 5-on-5, which is middling. His own expected goals, a measure of the quality of his shots, sit at 2.05 against 3 actual goals, so some of his scoring is running hot. Still, ANA's share of chances improves by about 4 points when he plays, and he is averaging 19.7 minutes a night, so the playmaking looks real. That matters for a 5-6-0 team that has been outplayed overall (46 percent of expected goals) and is leaning on goaltending. PHI, at 3-7-3, has been worse, with 41 percent of chances.
